cases.name: read-scoop-plain
cases.note: No version: the broker cannot pin one through Scoop.

cases.name: read-scoop-version-unreadable
cases.note: Control: read-scoop-plain.

cases.name: read-scoop-version-unreadable-uninstall
cases.note: Package.Version through Scoop is unreadable on an Uninstall too. Control: read-scoop-uninstall-plain.

cases.name: read-scoop-skip-hash-check
cases.note: '--skip-hash-check' would ask for SkipHashCheck, so the request is unreadable (§manager-scoop). Control: read-scoop-cluster-without-s.

cases.name: read-scoop-short-s
cases.note: '-s' would ask for SkipHashCheck, so the request is unreadable (§manager-scoop). Control: read-scoop-cluster-without-s.

cases.name: read-scoop-cluster-containing-s
cases.note: '-ks' would ask for SkipHashCheck, so the request is unreadable (§manager-scoop). Control: read-scoop-cluster-without-s.

cases.name: read-scoop-cluster-without-s
cases.note: A short cluster starts with one '-' followed by a character other than '-'.

cases.name: read-scoop-double-hyphen-s
cases.note: A short cluster starts with one '-' followed by a character other than '-'.

cases.name: read-scoop-long-prefix
cases.note: A short cluster starts with one '-' followed by a character other than '-'.

cases.name: read-scoop-no-hyphen
cases.note: 's' does not start with '-', so the request is unreadable (§manager-scoop). Control: read-scoop-cluster-without-s.

cases.name: read-scoop-architecture-field
cases.note: Package.Architecture is X64. The observer has one Allow rule per value and a catch-all; a known property also matches its value rule, while an unknown one matches none (§applicability), so only the catch-all applies to it.

cases.name: read-scoop-architecture-arch
cases.note: '--arch' names the option --arch, so the request is unreadable (§manager-scoop). Control: read-scoop-architecture-cluster-without-a.

cases.name: read-scoop-architecture-arch-alone
cases.note: '--arch' names the option --arch, so the request is unreadable (§manager-scoop). Control: read-scoop-architecture-cluster-without-a.

cases.name: read-scoop-architecture-short-a
cases.note: '-a' contains 'a' after its '-', so the request is unreadable (§manager-scoop). Control: read-scoop-architecture-cluster-without-a.

cases.name: read-scoop-architecture-cluster-containing-a
cases.note: '-ka' contains 'a' after its '-', so the request is unreadable (§manager-scoop). Control: read-scoop-architecture-cluster-without-a.

cases.name: read-scoop-architecture-cluster-without-a
cases.note: Package.Architecture is X64. The observer has one Allow rule per value and a catch-all; a known property also matches its value rule, while an unknown one matches none (§applicability), so only the catch-all applies to it.

cases.name: read-scoop-architecture-double-hyphen-a
cases.note: Package.Architecture is X64. The observer has one Allow rule per value and a catch-all; a known property also matches its value rule, while an unknown one matches none (§applicability), so only the catch-all applies to it.

cases.name: read-scoop-architecture-cluster-s-and-a
cases.note: '-sa' contains 'a' after its '-', so the request is unreadable (§manager-scoop). Control: read-scoop-architecture-cluster-without-a.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-url-untrusted-by-bucket
cases.note: A manifest URL is a known source, which a bucket selector does not match. Package.Id equals Source.Name, so the request is readable (§manager-scoop).

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-url-named
cases.note: A Source selector names the manifest URL with exact characters, so it matches (§manager-scoop). Control: read-scoop-manifest-url-named-any-case.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-url-named-any-case
cases.note: The trusted selector equals the manifest source only ignoring case, so it is unknown for it and does not trust it (§manager-scoop, §trusted-sources). Control: read-scoop-manifest-url-named.

cases.name: read-scoop-local-path-named
cases.note: A local path source is never readable: only an http:// or https:// manifest URL equal to Package.Id is (§manager-scoop). Control: read-scoop-manifest-url-named.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-url-any-source
cases.note: AnySource covers manifest URLs.

cases.name: read-scoop-skip-hash-check-upper
cases.note: '--SKIP-HASH-CHECK' would ask for SkipHashCheck, so the request is unreadable (§manager-scoop). An option name matches ignoring ASCII case. Control: read-scoop-skip-hash-check.

cases.name: read-scoop-short-upper-s
cases.note: '-S' would ask for SkipHashCheck, so the request is unreadable (§manager-scoop). '-S' is a short cluster containing 's', since names match ignoring ASCII case. Control: read-scoop-short-s.

cases.name: read-scoop-skip-hash-check-attached
cases.note: '--skip-hash-check=true' would ask for SkipHashCheck, so the request is unreadable (§manager-scoop). An option name ends at the element's first '=', so '--skip-hash-check=true' is '--skip-hash-check'. Control: read-scoop-skip-hash-check-longer-name.

cases.name: read-scoop-skip-hash-check-longer-name
cases.note: '--skip-hash-checks' is a longer name with '--skip-hash-check' as its prefix, not that option. Control: read-scoop-skip-hash-check-attached.

cases.name: read-scoop-cluster-hyphen-inside
cases.note: '-x-s' would ask for SkipHashCheck, so the request is unreadable (§manager-scoop). '-x-s' starts with one '-' followed by a character other than '-', so the whole element is one short cluster, and it contains 's'. Control: read-scoop-cluster-without-s.

cases.name: read-scoop-cluster-s-after-equals
cases.note: Every character of a short cluster after its '-', including '=' and what follows it, is an option name, so '-k=s' includes 's' and the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q-value-x.

cases.name: read-scoop-architecture-arch-attached
cases.note: '--arch=64bit' names the option --arch, since an option name ends at the first '=', so the request is unreadable (§manager-scoop). Control: read-scoop-architecture-cluster-without-a.

cases.name: read-scoop-architecture-arch-upper-attached
cases.note: '--ARCH=64bit' names the option --arch, since an option name ends at the first '=' and matches ignoring ASCII case, so the request is unreadable (§manager-scoop). Control: read-scoop-architecture-cluster-without-a.

cases.name: read-scoop-architecture-longer-name
cases.note: '--architecture=64bit' names '--architecture', a longer name with '--arch' as its prefix, which has no effect, so the architecture stays X64. Package.Architecture is X64. The observer has one Allow rule per value and a catch-all; a known property also matches its value rule, while an unknown one matches none (§applicability), so only the catch-all applies to it.

cases.name: read-scoop-architecture-short-upper-a
cases.note: '-A' contains 'a' ignoring ASCII case, so the request is unreadable (§manager-scoop). Control: read-scoop-architecture-cluster-without-a.

cases.name: read-scoop-uninstall-plain
cases.note: A readable Scoop Uninstall without a version; an Uninstall is never missing its version (§missing-version). Control for read-scoop-version-unreadable-uninstall, which adds Package.Version.

cases.name: read-scoop-bucket-app
cases.note: A bucket name and an app id of ASCII letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.' name one app in the bucket.

cases.name: read-scoop-bucket-id-json-suffix
cases.note: An id ending with '.json' would name a local manifest file. Control: read-scoop-bucket-app.

cases.name: read-scoop-bucket-id-json-suffix-upper
cases.note: An id ending with '.json' ignoring ASCII case is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-bucket-app.

cases.name: read-scoop-bucket-id-slash
cases.note: '/' in the id would name a path inside the bucket. Control: read-scoop-bucket-app.

cases.name: read-scoop-bucket-id-at-version
cases.note: '@' in the id would select a version after the app name. Control: read-scoop-bucket-app.

cases.name: read-scoop-bucket-name-colon
cases.note: 'https:' does not start with 'https://', so it is a bucket name, and ':' is not allowed in one. Control: read-scoop-bucket-app.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-ftp-other-id
cases.note: 'FTP://h/x.json' is a manifest URL ignoring ASCII case, so the id 'x' is not read as an app in a bucket, and an ftp URL is never readable. Control: read-scoop-bucket-app, whose source is a bucket.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-unc-source
cases.note: A source containing '\\' is a local path, and only an http:// or https:// manifest URL equal to Package.Id is readable. Control: read-scoop-bucket-app, whose source is a bucket.

cases.name: read-scoop-bucket-dot-dot
cases.note: '..' as a bucket ends with '.', so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-bucket-app.

cases.name: read-scoop-id-dot-dot
cases.note: '..' as an id ends with '.', so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-bucket-app.

cases.name: read-scoop-id-trailing-dot
cases.note: '7zip.' ends with '.', which Windows drops from a path segment, so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-bucket-app.

cases.name: read-scoop-source-trailing-dot
cases.note: 'main.' ends with '.', which Windows drops from a path segment, so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-plain.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-url-id-differs
cases.note: A manifest URL source whose Package.Id differs from it is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-manifest-url-any-source.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-url-id-only
cases.note: A Package.Id that is a manifest URL through a bucket source is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-manifest-url-any-source.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-url-id-differs-in-case
cases.note: Package.Id must equal Source.Name with exact characters. Control: read-scoop-manifest-url-any-source.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-ftp-equal
cases.note: An ftp manifest URL is never readable, even when Package.Id equals Source.Name. Control: read-scoop-manifest-http-equal.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-leading-slash-equal
cases.note: '/https://h/a.json' is a manifest URL once its leading '/' is removed, but Package.Id does not itself start with 'https://', so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-manifest-http-equal.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-http-equal
cases.note: An http:// manifest URL equal to Package.Id is readable.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-scheme-upper-equal
cases.note: 'HTTPS://' starts Package.Id ignoring ASCII case, so a manifest URL equal to Package.Id is readable.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-selector-other-case-allow
cases.note: The selector equals the manifest source only ignoring case, so it is unknown and the Allow rule fails closed. Control: read-scoop-manifest-selector-exact-allow.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-selector-exact-allow
cases.note: The selector equals the manifest source with exact characters, so it matches.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-selector-other-case-deny
cases.note: The selector equals the manifest source only ignoring case, so it is unknown and the Deny rule applies. Control: read-scoop-manifest-selector-other-url-deny.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-selector-other-url-deny
cases.note: A different manifest URL does not match the selector, so the Deny rule does not apply.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-trusted-other-case
cases.note: A trusted selector that equals the manifest source only ignoring case is unknown, so it does not trust the source. Control: read-scoop-manifest-trusted-exact.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-trusted-exact
cases.note: A trusted selector equal to the manifest source with exact characters trusts it.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-packages-other-case-allow
cases.note: A manifest id names itself and keeps its case, so a pattern equal to it only ignoring case makes Packages unknown and the Allow rule fails closed. Control: read-scoop-manifest-packages-exact-allow.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-packages-exact-allow
cases.note: A pattern equal to the manifest id with exact characters matches it.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-packages-scheme-case-deny
cases.note: The pattern equals the manifest id only ignoring case, so Packages is unknown and the Deny rule applies. Control: read-scoop-manifest-packages-other-url-deny.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-packages-other-url-deny
cases.note: A different manifest id does not match the pattern, so the Deny rule does not apply.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-id-at-userinfo
cases.note: Scoop would split the text after '@' off the URL as a version, so a manifest id containing '@', here in the URL's userinfo, is unreadable, and the Deny rule naming the whole URL is never reached. Control: read-scoop-manifest-id-without-at.

cases.name: read-scoop-bucket-app-case-folded
cases.note: A bucket's app names keep the lowercase canonical form, so 'Git' matches the pattern 'git'. Contrast read-scoop-manifest-packages-other-case-allow.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-global
cases.note: '--global' names the option --global, so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-all
cases.note: '--all' names the option --all, so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-global-upper
cases.note: '--GLOBAL' names --global ignoring ASCII case, so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-short-g
cases.note: '-g' contains 'g' after its '-', so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-short-upper-g
cases.note: '-G' contains 'g' ignoring ASCII case after its '-', so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-cluster-kg
cases.note: '-kg' contains 'g' after its '-', so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-cluster-qa
cases.note: '-qa' contains 'a' after its '-', so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-short-value-contains-g
cases.note: '-q=abcg' contains 'a' and 'g' in its text after '-', which includes the text after '=', so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-arch-upper-other-value
cases.note: '--ARCH=x' names --arch ignoring ASCII case, so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-terminator
cases.note: '--' is exactly '--', so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-white-space
cases.note: '--no-update-scoop ' contains U+0020, which has the White_Space property, so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-no-break-space
cases.note: '--x\u00a0y' contains U+00A0, which has the White_Space property, so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-globalx
cases.note: '--globalx' names --globalx, not --global, so the request is readable.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-single-hyphen
cases.note: '-' is exactly '-', which Scoop reads as another app, so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-short-q
cases.note: '-q' contains none of 'g', 'a' and 's', so the request is readable.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-short-q-value-s
cases.note: '-q=s' is an example the section gives: its option names are 'q', '=' and 's', so it would ask for SkipHashCheck and the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q-value-x.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-non-ascii-option-name
cases.note: '--s\u212aip-hash-check' has U+212A KELVIN SIGN in its option name, a code point above U+007F, so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-ascii-option-name.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-ascii-option-name
cases.note: '--sxip-hash-check' has only ASCII in its option name and names no option the Scoop reading refuses, so the request is readable.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-non-ascii-short-option
cases.note: '-\u212a' has U+212A in its option name, so the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-non-ascii-after-equals
cases.note: A long option's name ends at the first '=', and an element starting with '--' is not a short cluster, so U+212A after '=' leaves the request readable. Contrast read-scoop-parameter-non-ascii-option-name and read-scoop-parameter-short-non-ascii-after-equals.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-short-non-ascii-after-equals
cases.note: A short cluster that contains a code point above U+007F is unreadable, even after '=': '-q=' followed by U+212A. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q-value-x.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-options-end
cases.note: '--%' is exactly '--%', which ends Scoop's options, so Scoop would read a later element as another app and the request is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-options-end-suffixed.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-options-end-suffixed
cases.note: '--%x' is not exactly '--%' and names no refused option, so the request is readable. Contrast read-scoop-parameter-options-end.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-id-at-version
cases.note: Scoop would split '@1.0' off the URL as a version, fetch the shorter URL and generate that version, so a manifest id containing '@' is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-manifest-id-without-at.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-id-without-at
cases.note: The same URL without '@', equal to Source.Name, is a readable manifest Install.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-update-unreadable
cases.note: An Update whose Source.Name and Package.Id are a manifest URL is unreadable, because Scoop acts on an installed app it derives from the URL. Control: read-scoop-manifest-id-without-at, an Install.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-id-only-update-unreadable
cases.note: An Update whose Package.Id alone is a manifest URL is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-update-plain.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-uninstall-unreadable
cases.note: An Uninstall whose Source.Name and Package.Id are a manifest URL is unreadable, because Scoop acts on an installed app it derives from the URL. Control: read-scoop-manifest-id-without-at, an Install.

cases.name: read-scoop-manifest-id-only-uninstall-unreadable
cases.note: An Uninstall whose Package.Id alone is a manifest URL is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-uninstall-plain.

cases.name: read-scoop-install-source-selector-allow
cases.note: The source of a Scoop Install is known, so a Source selector naming it matches.

cases.name: read-scoop-install-source-selector-deny
cases.note: The source of a Scoop Install is known, so a Deny rule naming another source does not apply.

cases.name: read-scoop-install-trusted-named-source
cases.note: A TrustedSources entry naming the source of a Scoop Install trusts it.

cases.name: read-scoop-update-source-selector-allow
cases.note: The source of a Scoop Update is unknown, so a Source selector naming Source.Name is unknown and the Allow rule fails closed. Control: read-scoop-install-source-selector-allow.

cases.name: read-scoop-update-source-selector-deny
cases.note: The source of a Scoop Update is unknown, so a Deny rule naming another source still applies. Control: read-scoop-install-source-selector-deny.

cases.name: read-scoop-update-any-source-allow
cases.note: An AnySource selector matches the unknown source of a Scoop Update.

cases.name: read-scoop-update-trusted-named-source
cases.note: The source of a Scoop Update is unknown, so a TrustedSources entry naming Source.Name does not trust it, while AnySource does (read-scoop-update-any-source-allow). Control: read-scoop-install-trusted-named-source.

cases.name: read-scoop-uninstall-any-source-allow
cases.note: An AnySource selector matches the unknown source of a Scoop Uninstall.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-short-q-value-a
cases.note: '-q=a' has the option names 'q', '=' and 'a', and a short cluster naming 'a' is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q-value-x.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-short-q-value-g
cases.note: '-q=g' has the option names 'q', '=' and 'g', and a short cluster naming 'g' is unreadable. Control: read-scoop-parameter-short-q-value-x.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-short-q-value-x
cases.note: '-q=x' has the option names 'q', '=' and 'x', none of which the section refuses, so the request is readable. Contrast read-scoop-parameter-short-q-value-s.

cases.name: read-scoop-parameter-long-value-s
cases.note: A long option's name ends at the first '=', so '--q=s' names '--q' only and the request is readable. Contrast read-scoop-parameter-short-q-value-s.
